parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish باسور (basur), from Arabic بَاسُور (bāsūr), from Classical Syriac *ܒܳܨܘܿܪܴܐ (bāṣōrā, “sore, ulcer”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish برج (burc, “zodiac, constellation, tower”), from Arabic بُرْج (burj), from Classical Syriac ܒܘܪܓܐ (burgāʾ, “tower, columbarium”), from Ancient Greek πύργος (púrgos) or Latin burgus, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerǵʰ- (“high”) (compare English borough).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دجال, from Arabic دَجَّال (dajjāl), from Classical Syriac ܕܰܓܳܠܳܐ (daggālā, “liar”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فرعون (fir'avun), borrowed from Arabic فِرْعَوْن (firʕawn), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܦܹܪܥܘܼܢ, borrowed from Koine Greek Φαραών (Pharaṓn), borrowed from Biblical Hebrew פַּרְעֹה, borrowed from Egyptian pr-ꜥꜣ, from pr + ꜥꜣ.
From Ottoman Turkish خدمت (hidmet, hıdmet), خذمت (hizmet, hızmet), from Arabic خِدْمَة (ḵidma), from Classical Syriac ܚܕܡܬ.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ابریق (ibrik, ıbrık), borrowed from Arabic إِبْرِيق (ʔibrīq), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܒܪܝܩܐ (ʾaḇrēqā), possibly borrowed from Middle Persian *ābrēk, or possibly borrowed from Parthian *ābrēk.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اكسیر (iksir), from Arabic إِكْسِير (ʔiksīr), from Classical Syriac ܟܣܝܪܝܢ (ksīrīn), from Ancient Greek ξηρίον (xēríon, “medicinal powder”).

parole.significato: flax, a plant of the species Linum usitatissimum, cultivated as a food and fiber crop
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كتان (kettan, ketan), from Arabic كَتَّان (kattān, “flax; linen”), from Classical Syriac ܟܶܬܳܢܳܐ (kettānā, “flax; linen”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كابوس, borrowed from Arabic كَابُوس (kābūs), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܟܒܘܫܐ (kāḇōšā, “nightmare, incubus”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كانون اول (kanun-ı evvel), from Arabic كَانُون الأَوَّل (kānūn al-ʔawwal), from Classical Syriac ܟܢܘܢ ܐ. By surface analysis, kânun + evvel (“first”). The name was officially changed to Aralık by law number 4696 passed January 10, 1945.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كانون ثانی (kanun-ı sani), from Arabic كَانُونُ الثَّانِي (kānūnu ṯ-ṯānī), from Classical Syriac ܟܢܘܢ ܒ. By surface analysis, kânun + sani (“second”). The name was officially changed to Ocak by law number 4696 passed January 10, 1945.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كرسی (kürsi), from Arabic كُرْسِيّ (kursiyy), from Classical Syriac ܟܘܪܣܝܐ (kursəyā), from Akkadian 𒄑𒄖𒍝 (kussûm), from Sumerian 𒄑𒄖𒍝 (^(g̃eš)gu-za /⁠guza⁠/, “chair”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوشنه (küşne, “kind of vetch”), from Arabic كُشْنَى (kušnā, “Vicia palaestina”), ultimately from Classical Syriac ܟܘܫܢܐ (kūšnā).

parole.significato: coral, coralline, resembling or made of coral
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مرجان (mercan), from Old Anatolian Turkish مرجان (mercān), from Arabic مَرْجَان (marjān), from Classical Syriac ܡܪܰܓܳܢ (margān, “pearl-like”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ناموس (namus), from Arabic نَامُوس (nāmūs), from Classical Syriac ܢܡܘܣܐ (nāmōsā), from Ancient Greek νόμος (nómos).

parole.significato: callus, corn, a hardened area of the skin, especially on the foot or hand
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ناصور (nasır, “corn, callus”), from Arabic نَاصُور (nāṣūr, “fistula”), ultimately from Classical Syriac ܢܳܨܘܿܪܴܐ (nāṣōrā, “sore, ulcer”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نیسان (nisan), borrowed from Arabic نَيْسَان (naysān), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܢܝܣܢ (nīsān), from Aramaic נִיסָן (nīsān), borrowed from Akkadian 𒌚𒁈 (nisannum).

parole.significato: kind of shallow, wide basket made of wicker
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سله (sele), from Arabic سَلَّة (salla, “basket”), ultimately from Classical Syriac ܣܲܠܛܵܐ (sallətā, “basket”).

parole.significato: sumac, any of various shrubs or small trees of the genus Rhus and its fruit
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سماق (sumak, somak), from Arabic سُمَّاق (summāq, “sumac”), ultimately from Classical Syriac ܣܘܡܩܐ (summāqā, “red; sumac”).

From Ottoman Turkish تابوت (tabut), from Arabic تَابُوت (tābūt), from Classical Syriac ܬܝܒܘܬܐ (tēḇūṯā), ultimately from Egyptian DbA-t:pr ḏbꜣt (“sarcophagus, coffin”) or T-b-O39 ṯb (“chest, box”). Compare Demotic Egyptian tbyt (“sarcophagus, shrine, chest”), dbt, and tbt (“chest”) and Coptic ⲧⲁⲓⲃⲉ (

From Ottoman Turkish تموز (temmuz), from Arabic تَمُّوز (tammūz), from Classical Syriac ܬܡܘܙ (tāmūz), from Aramaic תַּמּוּז (tāmuz), from Akkadian 𒌗𒋗 (ⁱᵗⁱDuʾzu/Dūzu), from Sumerian 𒌉𒍣 (DUMU.ZID, “the true son”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترجمان, from Arabic تَرْجُمَان (tarjumān), Classical Syriac ܬܰܪܓܡܳܢܳܐ (targmānā, “interpreter”), from Akkadian 𒅴𒁄 (targumannum, “interpreter”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زرافه (zürafa), from Arabic زَرَافَة (zarāfa), from Classical Syriac ܙܪܢܦܐ (zarnāp̄ā), from Classical Persian زُرنَاپَا (zurnāpā). Etymologically related to zurna and piyade.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شباط (şubat), from Arabic شُبَاط (šubāṭ), from Classical Syriac ܫܒܛ.
